1-1.text: Part one. Types of angle. ... An angle measures a turn. We measure angles in degrees, written with a little circle. One full turn is 360 degrees.

1-2.text: A right angle is a quarter turn: exactly 90 degrees. We mark it with a little square.

1-3.text: An acute angle is less than 90 degrees. An obtuse angle is more than 90 degrees but less than 180 degrees.

1-4.text: A straight line makes an angle of 180 degrees. A reflex angle is more than 180 degrees but less than 360 degrees.

2-1.text: Part two. Angle rules. ... Angles on a straight line add up to 180 degrees. One angle is 115 degrees, so the other is x equals 180 minus 115, which is 65 degrees.

2-2.text: Angles round a point add up to 360 degrees. 100 plus 140 is 240 degrees, so y equals 360 minus 240, which is 120 degrees.

2-3.text: The angles in a triangle add up to 180 degrees. 40 plus 75 is 115 degrees, so x equals 180 minus 115, which is 65 degrees.

2-4.text: The angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360 degrees. Why? Cut it into two triangles: 2 times 180 is 360 degrees.

3-1.text: Part three. Crossing and parallel lines. ... When two straight lines cross, the angles opposite each other are equal. They are called vertically opposite angles.

3-2.text: Parallel lines go in the same direction and never meet, like train tracks. We mark them with little arrows.

3-3.text: Draw a line across two parallel lines. The angles inside a Z shape are alternate angles. Alternate angles are equal.

3-4.text: The angles in an F shape are corresponding angles. They are equal too.

3-5.text: The angles inside a C or U shape are co-interior angles. They add up to 180 degrees: 55 plus 125 is 180 degrees.

4-1.text: Part four. Polygons. ... A polygon is a flat shape with straight sides. A triangle has 3 sides, a quadrilateral 4, a pentagon 5, a hexagon 6 and an octagon 8.

4-2.text: In a regular polygon, all the sides are the same length and all the angles are the same size.

4-3.text: The angles inside a hexagon add up to 720 degrees. A regular hexagon has 6 equal angles, so each one is 720 divided by 6, which is 120 degrees.

4-4.text: Walk all the way round a polygon and you make one full turn. So the exterior angles add up to 360 degrees. Each exterior angle of a regular hexagon is 360 divided by 6, which is 60 degrees.

4-5.text: An interior angle and its exterior angle sit on a straight line, so they add up to 180 degrees: 120 plus 60 is 180 degrees.

5-1.text: Part five. Properties of shapes. ... Triangles: an equilateral triangle has 3 equal sides, an isosceles triangle has 2 equal sides, and a scalene triangle has no equal sides.

5-2.text: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. A rectangle has 4 right angles. A rhombus has 4 equal sides, like a square pushed over.

5-3.text: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. A trapezium has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

5-4.text: A line of symmetry is a mirror line: fold along it and the two halves match. A square has 4 lines of symmetry. A rectangle has 2.

5-5.text: 3D shapes have faces, edges and vertices (corners). A triangular prism has 5 faces, 9 edges and 6 vertices.
